---
title: "Subjects in the picture"
description: "What Frame Job finds in a clip's picture on this Mac, what it doesn't know about the people in it, and when a file gets analysed."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Frame Job can find who and what is in a clip's picture: faces, people and the parts the eye goes to first. Its framing tools use this to keep a subject in shot on a canvas of a different shape.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['Clip ▸ Follow Subject…', 'File ▸ Make Vertical Version…', 'View ▸ Show Subjects']}
  tools={['get_media_analysis', 'reframe_clip', 'make_vertical_version']}
  needs="Nothing. Apple's Vision framework does this on your Mac, with no key and no upload."
/>

## What is found

Frame Job looks at the picture ten times a second of the file's own time, so a clip you've slowed down or sped up doesn't change what's found. It keeps three things from each look.

### Faces

Each face's box, how it's turned, and how open the mouth is. Faces in a sample are listed from left to right. See [Faces](/projects/media-analysis/#faces) under media analysis.

### People

Each person's head and shoulders, as a box. A person's box stays useful when the face is turned away or hidden.

### Salient regions

The parts of the picture the eye goes to first, as boxes. In a talking-head shot this is usually the speaker. On a slide it's often the text. See [People and salient regions](/projects/media-analysis/#people-and-salient-regions) under media analysis.

[Show Subjects](/framing/show-subjects/) draws all three over the preview, so you can see what Frame Job has to work with.

## Boxes, not people

Each sample stands alone. A box has no name, and nothing records that a box in one sample is the same person as a box in the next. Frame Job never puts a name to a face, and it doesn't recognise anyone.

[Follow Subject](/framing/follow-subject/#which-subject-it-follows) works out who's who for itself each time it plans, from how the boxes overlap from one sample to the next. That reasoning isn't kept, and it stops at a shot change. Someone who leaves the shot for more than a second and comes back counts as someone new.

## When a file is analysed

Importing a file doesn't analyse its picture. A file is analysed when something asks for it:

- **Clip ▸ Follow Subject…**
- **File ▸ Make Vertical Version…**
- An agent, with `get_media_analysis` or `reframe_clip`

Those framing commands ask only for the part of the file each clip plays, plus a second either side. **View ▸ Show Subjects** never asks, so turning it on costs nothing.

Analysis runs in the background and keeps what it has found if it's stopped. Asking again continues from there, and a part that's already been analysed isn't read again. What's found is kept in the project's cache, so a file is only analysed once.

[On-device media analysis](/projects/media-analysis/#analysis-happens-on-demand) covers this in full, including [the Analyzing sheet](/projects/media-analysis/#the-analyzing-sheet) and [how background jobs run](/projects/media-analysis/#analysis-runs-in-the-background).

## What uses it

| Feature | What it uses |
| --- | --- |
| [Follow Subject](/framing/follow-subject/) | Faces, people and salient regions, to frame the selected clips |
| [Make Vertical Version](/framing/make-vertical-version/) | The same, to frame a whole timeline on a tall or square canvas |
| [Follow the speaker in a vertical](/framing/follow-speaker/) | Faces and how open each mouth is, to match each microphone to a face |
| [Cut from faces with one microphone](/multicam/one-microphone/) | Faces and how open each mouth is, to tell who's talking |
| [Show Subjects](/framing/show-subjects/) | All three, drawn over the preview |

An agent can frame a clip with the same analysis. See [Reframe a clip (agents)](/framing/reframe-clip/).

## Related

- [Show Subjects](/framing/show-subjects/)
- [Follow Subject](/framing/follow-subject/)
- [On-device media analysis](/projects/media-analysis/)

---
title: "Show Subjects"
description: "Draw the faces, people and salient regions Frame Job has found for a clip over the preview, so you can see what framing will follow."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Show Subjects outlines what Frame Job has found in the selected clip at the playhead, right on the preview. Use it to check what [Follow Subject](/framing/follow-subject/) has to work with.

<AtAGlance
  menu="View ▸ Show Subjects"
  needs="Nothing. It only draws what has already been found."
/>

## Turn on Show Subjects

<Steps>

1. Select a clip of a movie.

2. Move the playhead to a moment that clip shows.

3. Choose **View ▸ Show Subjects**. A tick appears beside it in the menu.

</Steps>

Select another clip to see its boxes, and move the playhead to see another moment. Choose the item again to turn it off.

The item has no shortcut and is always available.

It draws for one clip at a time. With several clips selected, that's the front-most one showing at the playhead. A selected still, picture, nest, text, shape or graphic draws nothing and shows no note, and neither does a clip the playhead isn't on.

## What the outlines mean

| Outline | What it marks |
| --- | --- |
| Yellow | A face |
| Teal | A person's head and shoulders |
| Purple, dashed | A salient region, a part of the picture the eye goes to first |

Each outline has a dark line behind it, so it stays visible on a bright picture. Faces draw on top of the other two.

[Subjects in the picture](/framing/what-is-found/) explains what each kind of box is.

## The boxes stay on the picture

The boxes sit on the clip's picture wherever you've placed it. If you've moved, scaled or rotated the clip, each box moves and turns with it. If you've cropped the clip, the boxes are clipped to the crop.

They also follow the clip's speed, speed ramps and reversal, so they show what the clip is showing at that moment rather than what's at the same time in the file.

## Not analyzed

When nothing has been found for the clip's picture at the playhead, a note sits at the clip's top-left corner:

> Not analyzed — Clip ▸ Follow Subject… analyzes it

Show Subjects never starts an analysis, so turning it on costs nothing. To make the boxes, run [Follow Subject](/framing/follow-subject/) or [Make Vertical Version](/framing/make-vertical-version/) on the clip. If Show Subjects is on when an analysis lands, the boxes appear by themselves.

Three situations are worth knowing:

- Analysis covers the parts of a file that clips play, plus a second either side. Another part of the same file can still read "Not analyzed".
- A part that's been analysed and holds nothing shows no outlines and no note.
- Follow Subject doesn't analyse a screen recording that has its [cursor file](/recording/cursor-files/), so the note stays on such a clip. See [Screen recordings are skipped](/framing/follow-subject/#screen-recordings-are-skipped).

## A view of the window

Show Subjects belongs to the window, not the project.

- It's off in a new window, and each window has its own setting.
- It isn't remembered between launches.
- It edits nothing, so it isn't an undo step.
- It never changes an export or a saved frame.

## With an agent

There's no agent tool for the overlay. An agent reads the same boxes with `get_media_analysis`. See [Tools: reading analysis](/mcp/tools-analysis/).

## Related

- [Subjects in the picture](/framing/what-is-found/)
- [Follow Subject](/framing/follow-subject/)
- [On-device media analysis](/projects/media-analysis/)

---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

<AtAGlance
  menu="Clip ▸ Follow Subject…"
  where="Each move, on the clip's action lane"
  tools="reframe_clip"
  needs="Nothing. Faces, people and shot changes are found on your Mac, with no key and no upload."
/>

## Frame clips on their subject

<Steps>

1. Set the canvas you want first, in the [Document tab](/projects/canvas-size/). Follow Subject doesn't change the canvas.

2. Select the clips to frame.

3. Choose **Clip ▸ Follow Subject…**. It's available when a selected clip plays a movie and no sheet is open, inside a nest too. There's no keyboard shortcut.

4. Set [Follow](#follow), [Zoom](#zoom) and [Where Empty](#where-empty).

5. Read [the summary](#the-summary) under the controls, which says what will happen.

6. Choose **Follow** (<kbd>Return</kbd>), or **Cancel** (<kbd>Esc</kbd>) to leave everything as it was.

</Steps>

<Shot
  name="15i-follow-subject-sheet.sheet"
  alt="The Follow Subject sheet, with Follow set to Subject, Zoom at 125 percent and Where Empty set to Show Whole. A summary reads: Finds the faces, people and shot changes in 1 file on this Mac first, then frames 1 clip. Cancel and Follow buttons sit at the bottom right."
/>

:::tip
To change the canvas and frame a whole timeline in one go, use [Make Vertical Version](/framing/make-vertical-version/) instead.
:::

A still, a picture, a nest, text, a shape, a graphic or an adjustment clip in the selection is left alone, with no line in the summary.

## The controls

### Follow

Follow chooses what the frame stays on.

| Choice | What the frame follows |
| --- | --- |
| **Subject** | A face, or where there's none a person, or where there's neither the region the eye goes to. This is the default. |
| **Faces** | Faces only |
| **People** | People only |
| **Salient Region** | Salient regions only |
| **Center** | Nothing. The frame holds on the middle of the picture for the whole clip, with no analysis needed. |

### Zoom

Zoom sets how tight the frame is, in whole percents from 100 to 400. At 100 % the picture just covers the canvas.

It starts at 100 %. If the first selected clip's picture is within 1 % of the canvas's shape, it starts at 125 % instead, because at 100 % such a picture fills the canvas exactly and the frame has no room to move.

Zoom enlarges the picture, and so does putting a landscape picture on a tall canvas. A 1080p source on a 1080 × 1920 canvas is already enlarged ×1.78 at 100 %, which can look soft on a phone.

### Where Empty

Where Empty sets what the frame shows while there's nothing to follow.

| Choice | What shows |
| --- | --- |
| **Show Whole** | The whole picture, with a [blurred copy](#the-blurred-backgrounds-track) filling the canvas around it. This is the default. |
| **Center** | The middle of the picture, at the same zoom |

It's dimmed while Follow is **Center**.

### What's remembered

**Follow** and **Where Empty** are remembered for next time, and [Make Vertical Version](/framing/make-vertical-version/) shares them. They're saved when you choose **Follow**, even if you then stop the analysis, and never on **Cancel**. **Zoom** isn't remembered.

## The summary

Under the controls, the sheet says what **Follow** will do. It updates as you change a control, and after you leave the Zoom field.

| The sheet says | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| "Frames 2 clips." | How many clips will change. |
| "Adds a Backgrounds track for the blurred copy." | Some of the framing shows the whole picture, so a [blurred copy](#the-blurred-backgrounds-track) goes behind it. |
| "Adds 1 more track behind it where clips overlap." | Two selected clips overlap in time, so their copies need separate tracks. |
| "2 actions re-eased at a cut." | A shot change landed inside actions the clip already had, and each was split there and eased again on either side. See [It starts from the whole picture](#it-starts-from-the-whole-picture). |
| "1 action carries a framing move." | A move couldn't fit between the clip's own actions, so one of them carries it. |
| "Clip 3 is already framed this way." | That clip wouldn't change. |
| "Clip 3: …" | That clip can't be framed, and this is why. See [Clips it cannot frame](#clips-it-cannot-frame). |
| "Reading the analysis…" | Frame Job is loading what it found earlier. **Follow** is dimmed until it's done. |
| "Finds the faces, people and shot changes in 1 file on this Mac first, then frames 1 clip." | The [analysis comes first](#analysis-first). |

**Follow** is dimmed when nothing would change.

"Clip 3" uses Frame Job's own number for the clip, which isn't its position on the timeline.

## Analysis first

When the clips haven't been analysed, choosing **Follow** closes the sheet and opens the [Analyzing sheet](/projects/media-analysis/#the-analyzing-sheet) while Frame Job finds what it needs on your Mac. It then frames the clips by itself.

The Analyzing sheet has a row for each file and each kind of analysis: **Shot changes**, **Faces**, and **People and salient regions**. Only the part of each file the clip plays is read, plus a second either side.

**Stop** changes nothing. **Center** needs no analysis, so it frames at once.

Frame Job beeps and frames nothing in these cases, and says why at the foot of the inspector:

| The inspector says | What happened |
| --- | --- |
| "the project changed while Follow Subject was analyzing, so nothing was framed. Choose Follow Subject again." | The project changed, or you went into or out of a nest, while the analysis ran. What was found is kept, so a second try doesn't start over. |
| "The faces analysis of “interview.mov” failed: …" | An analysis couldn't finish. The sentence names the kind and the file. |

## It starts from the whole picture

Each clip is framed from the whole picture. Its own positions and scales are replaced, both the clip's base values and any an action sets. An action left with nothing to do is removed. The clip's volume and its other actions stay, and so does its crop, which the frame stays inside.

The moves then fit around the actions that remain:

- A move goes in a gap between them.
- A move that would overlap an action starts up to 0.5 s earlier to clear it.
- A move that still can't clear is carried by the action it overlaps, along that action's curve.
- A shot change that lands inside an action cuts it in three around the one-frame cut. A steady (linear) action plays as it did, and an eased one is eased again on each side.
- A speed action, or an action a trim left running past the clip's end, is never cut. It carries the change instead.

## How following moves

The frame never leaves the picture, so it doesn't show past the picture's edge while it follows.

### Which subject it follows

When several faces or people are in view, Frame Job scores each on how steadily it's there, how big it is and how central it is, over the second either side and within the shot.

It stays with its choice. Another subject takes over only after scoring at least 25 % better for 2 s, so two similar faces don't trade the frame back and forth. With **Subject**, a person's body stands in for their face while the face is turned away.

Only the first eight of each kind in a sample count. For faces, that's the eight furthest left.

### Where the subject sits

| Subject | Where it sits |
| --- | --- |
| A face | In the middle of the frame, or 38 % of the way down on a frame taller than wide, leaving room below for the rest of the person |
| A person | With the top of their box 12 % of the way down the frame |
| A salient region | In the middle of the frame |

### Easing and staying put

The frame eases onto the subject and moves only when the subject leaves the middle of the frame, so a speaker who sways stays put. The middle counts as 15 % of the frame's width and 12 % of its height either side.

A move travels at 0.8 frame widths a second and takes at least 0.4 s. No move starts within 0.5 s of the last one's end, unless the subject has left the frame altogether.

### At a shot change

The frame cuts with the picture, landing on the first frame of the new shot. It's placed on where the subject sits over the new shot's first second. No move runs across a cut.

### When the subject is lost

The frame holds for a second, so a blink or a turned head changes nothing. It then follows someone else in the shot if there's anyone. If not, it eases over 0.8 s to your [Where Empty](#where-empty) choice.

It comes back once a subject has been in view for 0.6 s.

A clip with nobody in view during its first second opens on Where Empty. A clip with nothing to follow at all stays on Where Empty for its whole length.

### Two people

The frame holds two faces or two people together when both fit in it. Each box is widened by 15 % before they're tested against the frame. Salient regions aren't paired.

## The blurred Backgrounds track

Where the frame shows the whole picture, the canvas shows around it. So a blurred copy of the clip goes on a new track named **Backgrounds** at the back, for the clip's whole length. That's the same copy [**Clip ▸ Add Blurred Background**](/canvas/backgrounds/#blurred-background) makes: picture only, filling the canvas.

No track is added when no clip needs one, which is always the case with **Center** for Follow or Where Empty. Where two selected clips overlap in time, the second copy goes on a further new track behind Backgrounds.

A clip with speed actions keeps them on its copy, so the copy shows the same frames.

## Every move is an action

Every move is an ordinary action on the clip's [action lane](/motion/action-lane/). To nudge where a frame ends, select the action and [drag the picture on the canvas](/motion/edit-an-action/#edit-on-the-canvas). You can move, resize or remove it as you would any other.

## Undo

**Edit ▸ Undo Follow Subject** takes the whole command back in one step, every clip and track included. What was found stays in the cache.

## Screen recordings are skipped

A screen recording Frame Job made, with its [cursor file](/recording/cursor-files/), isn't followed by faces, because a face on a screen isn't what the viewer is looking at. Follow Subject leaves it unanalysed and lists it under the summary:

> Clip 3: clip 3's media has a cursor file, so it follows the cursor, not faces; frame it with cursor, center, fit or keep

Of those, the sheet offers **Center**. [Make Vertical Version](/framing/make-vertical-version/) follows the pointer instead, and an agent can [follow it too](/framing/reframe-clip/).

## Clips it cannot frame

A selected movie clip that can't be followed gets a line under the summary, and the others are still framed. With no clip left to frame, the summary shows only those lines and **Follow** stays dimmed.

| Clip | The line says | What you can do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| On a matte track | "clip 3 is on a matte track, which framing would move; only keep reframes it" | Change the track's [matte setting](/canvas/matte-tracks/) or move the clip |
| Cut by a matte | "clip 3 is cut by the matte on track 7, which framing would move it out of; only keep reframes it" | The same |
| Rotated | "clip 3 is turned 15°, and framing works on an upright picture; only keep reframes it" | Set its [rotation](/canvas/transform/) back to 0° |
| Turned by an action | "clip 3's action 12 turns it, and framing works on an upright picture; only keep reframes it" | Take rotation out of [that action](/motion/edit-an-action/#take-a-property-out-of-the-action) |
| Spinning | "clip 3 spins in its motion, and framing works on an upright picture; only keep reframes it" | Remove the spin [preset](/motion/motion-presets/) |
| Cropped or scaled to nothing | "clip 3's crop or scale leaves no picture to frame" | Fix its [crop](/canvas/crop/) or scale |
| With a cursor file | See [above](#screen-recordings-are-skipped) | Choose **Center** |
| With no analysis under it | "clip 3 has no subjects to follow; analyze it first" | Lengthen the clip, or analyse its file again. A clip shorter than the gap between two samples can land here. |

"keep" and the other lowercase words in these lines are an agent's options. See [Reframe a clip (agents)](/framing/reframe-clip/).

A clip with nobody in it isn't one of these. It's framed on your [Where Empty](#where-empty) choice.

When an analysis has to run first, the sheet can't list these lines yet. Afterwards the clips that can be framed are framed, and the rest stay as they were with no message. If none can be, Frame Job beeps and shows the lines at the foot of the inspector.

- If a clip's file is missing or can't be read, the summary says so and **Follow** stays dimmed. [Relink it](/projects/relink-media/), or choose **Center**, which doesn't read the file.

- Running Follow Subject again on a clip whose frame shows the whole picture adds another Backgrounds track and another copy, and the first copy stays. Undo the first run, or delete the old copy.
- Inside a [nest](/editing/nests/), the nest's canvas is the canvas, and the Backgrounds track goes in the nest.
- A clip's speed, speed ramps and reversal are all taken into account, so the frame moves with what the clip shows.

## With an agent

`reframe_clip` frames one clip at a time. Follow Subject is that tool run on each selected clip, starting from the whole picture, with a Backgrounds track behind.

An agent has more choices than the sheet. It can show the whole picture, rescale a clip from the canvas it was made for, follow a recorded pointer or follow whoever's talking, and it can compose the framing into a clip's own moves instead of replacing them. See [Reframe a clip (agents)](/framing/reframe-clip/) and [Tools: framing and vertical](/mcp/tools-framing/).

## Related

- [Subjects in the picture](/framing/what-is-found/)
- [Show Subjects](/framing/show-subjects/)
- [Make Vertical Version](/framing/make-vertical-version/)
- [Backgrounds](/canvas/backgrounds/)
- [Actions](/motion/actions/)

- If a clip's file is missing or can't be read, the summary says so and **Follow** stays dimmed. [Relink it](/projects/relink-media/), or choose **Center**, which doesn't read the file.
- Follow Subject doesn't frame stills or pictures. [Make Vertical Version](/framing/make-vertical-version/) centres those.
- Running Follow Subject again on a clip whose frame shows the whole picture adds another Backgrounds track and another copy, and the first copy stays. Undo the first run, or delete the old copy.
- Inside a [nest](/editing/nests/), the nest's canvas is the canvas, and the Backgrounds track goes in the nest.
- A clip's speed, speed ramps and reversal are all taken into account, so the frame moves with what the clip shows.

## With an agent

`reframe_clip` frames one clip at a time. Follow Subject is that tool run on each selected clip, starting from the whole picture, with a Backgrounds track behind.

An agent has more choices than the sheet. It can show the whole picture, rescale a clip from the canvas it was made for, follow a recorded pointer or follow whoever's talking, and it can compose the framing into a clip's own moves instead of replacing them. See [Reframe a clip (agents)](/framing/reframe-clip/) and [Tools: framing and vertical](/mcp/tools-framing/).

input.content:
---
title: "Subjects in the picture"
description: "What Frame Job finds in a clip's picture on this Mac, what it doesn't know about the people in it, and when a file gets analysed."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Frame Job can find who and what is in a clip's picture: faces, people and the parts the eye goes to first. Its framing tools use this to keep a subject in shot on a canvas of a different shape.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['Clip ▸ Follow Subject…', 'File ▸ Make Vertical Version…', 'View ▸ Show Subjects']}
  tools={['get_media_analysis', 'reframe_clip', 'make_vertical_version']}
  needs="Nothing. Apple's Vision framework does this on your Mac, with no key and no upload."
/>

## What is found

Frame Job looks at the picture ten times a second of the file's own time, so a clip you've slowed down or sped up doesn't change what's found. It keeps three things from each look.

### Faces

Each face's box, how it's turned, and how open the mouth is. Faces in a sample are listed from left to right. See [Faces](/projects/media-analysis/#faces) under media analysis.

### People

Each person's head and shoulders, as a box. A person's box stays useful when the face is turned away or hidden.

### Salient regions

The parts of the picture the eye goes to first, as boxes. In a talking-head shot this is usually the speaker. On a slide it's often the text. See [People and salient regions](/projects/media-analysis/#people-and-salient-regions) under media analysis.

[Show Subjects](/framing/show-subjects/) draws all three over the preview, so you can see what Frame Job has to work with.

## Boxes, not people

Each sample stands alone. A box has no name, and nothing records that a box in one sample is the same person as a box in the next. Frame Job never puts a name to a face, and it doesn't recognise anyone.

[Follow Subject](/framing/follow-subject/#which-subject-it-follows) works out who's who for itself each time it plans, from how the boxes overlap from one sample to the next. That reasoning isn't kept, and it stops at a shot change. Someone who leaves the shot for more than a second and comes back counts as someone new.

## When a file is analysed

Importing a file doesn't analyse its picture. A file is analysed when something asks for it:

- **Clip ▸ Follow Subject…**
- **File ▸ Make Vertical Version…**
- An agent, with `get_media_analysis` or `reframe_clip`

Those framing commands ask only for the part of the file each clip plays, plus a second either side. **View ▸ Show Subjects** never asks, so turning it on costs nothing.

Analysis runs in the background and keeps what it has found if it's stopped. Asking again continues from there, and a part that's already been analysed isn't read again. What's found is kept in the project's cache, so a file is only analysed once.

[On-device media analysis](/projects/media-analysis/#analysis-happens-on-demand) covers this in full, including [the Analyzing sheet](/projects/media-analysis/#the-analyzing-sheet) and [how background jobs run](/projects/media-analysis/#analysis-runs-in-the-background).

## What uses it

| Feature | What it uses |
| --- | --- |
| [Follow Subject](/framing/follow-subject/) | Faces, people and salient regions, to frame the selected clips |
| [Make Vertical Version](/framing/make-vertical-version/) | The same, to frame a whole timeline on a tall or square canvas |
| [Follow the speaker in a vertical](/framing/follow-speaker/) | Faces and how open each mouth is, to match each microphone to a face |
| [Cut from faces with one microphone](/multicam/one-microphone/) | Faces and how open each mouth is, to tell who's talking |
| [Show Subjects](/framing/show-subjects/) | All three, drawn over the preview |

An agent can frame a clip with the same analysis. See [Reframe a clip (agents)](/framing/reframe-clip/).

## Related

- [Show Subjects](/framing/show-subjects/)
- [Follow Subject](/framing/follow-subject/)
- [On-device media analysis](/projects/media-analysis/)

---
title: "Show Subjects"
description: "Draw the faces, people and salient regions Frame Job has found for a clip over the preview, so you can see what framing will follow."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Show Subjects outlines what Frame Job has found in the selected clip at the playhead, right on the preview. Use it to check what [Follow Subject](/framing/follow-subject/) has to work with.

<AtAGlance
  menu="View ▸ Show Subjects"
  needs="Nothing. It only draws what has already been found."
/>

## Turn on Show Subjects

<Steps>

1. Select a clip of a movie.

2. Move the playhead to a moment that clip shows.

3. Choose **View ▸ Show Subjects**. A tick appears beside it in the menu.

</Steps>

Select another clip to see its boxes, and move the playhead to see another moment. Choose the item again to turn it off.

The item has no shortcut and is always available.

It draws for one clip at a time. With several clips selected, that's the front-most one showing at the playhead. A selected still, picture, nest, text, shape or graphic draws nothing and shows no note, and neither does a clip the playhead isn't on.

## What the outlines mean

| Outline | What it marks |
| --- | --- |
| Yellow | A face |
| Teal | A person's head and shoulders |
| Purple, dashed | A salient region, a part of the picture the eye goes to first |

Each outline has a dark line behind it, so it stays visible on a bright picture. Faces draw on top of the other two.

[Subjects in the picture](/framing/what-is-found/) explains what each kind of box is.

## The boxes stay on the picture

The boxes sit on the clip's picture wherever you've placed it. If you've moved, scaled or rotated the clip, each box moves and turns with it. If you've cropped the clip, the boxes are clipped to the crop.

They also follow the clip's speed, speed ramps and reversal, so they show what the clip is showing at that moment rather than what's at the same time in the file.

## Not analyzed

When nothing has been found for the clip's picture at the playhead, a note sits at the clip's top-left corner:

> Not analyzed — Clip ▸ Follow Subject… analyzes it

Show Subjects never starts an analysis, so turning it on costs nothing. To make the boxes, run [Follow Subject](/framing/follow-subject/) or [Make Vertical Version](/framing/make-vertical-version/) on the clip. If Show Subjects is on when an analysis lands, the boxes appear by themselves.

Three situations are worth knowing:

- Analysis covers the parts of a file that clips play, plus a second either side. Another part of the same file can still read "Not analyzed".
- A part that's been analysed and holds nothing shows no outlines and no note.
- Follow Subject doesn't analyse a screen recording that has its [cursor file](/recording/cursor-files/), so the note stays on such a clip. See [Screen recordings are skipped](/framing/follow-subject/#screen-recordings-are-skipped).

## A view of the window

Show Subjects belongs to the window, not the project.

- It's off in a new window, and each window has its own setting.
- It isn't remembered between launches.
- It edits nothing, so it isn't an undo step.
- It never changes an export or a saved frame.

## With an agent

There's no agent tool for the overlay. An agent reads the same boxes with `get_media_analysis`. See [Tools: reading analysis](/mcp/tools-analysis/).

## Related

- [Subjects in the picture](/framing/what-is-found/)
- [Follow Subject](/framing/follow-subject/)
- [On-device media analysis](/projects/media-analysis/)

---
title: "Follow Subject"
description: "Frame the selected movie clips on the person or thing in them, with eased moves you can edit and a blurred copy behind where the whole picture shows."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

Follow Subject keeps the person in shot when a clip's picture doesn't fit the canvas, such as a landscape recording on a 1080 × 1920 vertical canvas. It finds the subject, moves the frame with it, and writes each move as an ordinary action you can change.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Clip ▸ Follow Subject…"
  where="Each move, on the clip's action lane"
  tools="reframe_clip"
  needs="Nothing. Faces, people and shot changes are found on your Mac, with no key and no upload."
/>

## Frame clips on their subject

<Steps>

1. Set the canvas you want first, in the [Document tab](/projects/canvas-size/). Follow Subject doesn't change the canvas.

2. Select the clips to frame.

3. Choose **Clip ▸ Follow Subject…**. It's available when a selected clip plays a movie and no sheet is open, inside a nest too. There's no keyboard shortcut.

4. Set [Follow](#follow), [Zoom](#zoom) and [Where Empty](#where-empty).

5. Read [the summary](#the-summary) under the controls, which says what will happen.

6. Choose **Follow** (<kbd>Return</kbd>), or **Cancel** (<kbd>Esc</kbd>) to leave everything as it was.

</Steps>

<Shot
  name="15i-follow-subject-sheet.sheet"
  alt="The Follow Subject sheet, with Follow set to Subject, Zoom at 125 percent and Where Empty set to Show Whole. A summary reads: Finds the faces, people and shot changes in 1 file on this Mac first, then frames 1 clip. Cancel and Follow buttons sit at the bottom right."
/>

:::tip
To change the canvas and frame a whole timeline in one go, use [Make Vertical Version](/framing/make-vertical-version/) instead.
:::

A still, a picture, a nest, text, a shape, a graphic or an adjustment clip in the selection is left alone, with no line in the summary.

## The controls

### Follow

Follow chooses what the frame stays on.

| Choice | What the frame follows |
| --- | --- |
| **Subject** | A face, or where there's none a person, or where there's neither the region the eye goes to. This is the default. |
| **Faces** | Faces only |
| **People** | People only |
| **Salient Region** | Salient regions only |
| **Center** | Nothing. The frame holds on the middle of the picture for the whole clip, with no analysis needed. |

### Zoom

Zoom sets how tight the frame is, in whole percents from 100 to 400. At 100 % the picture just covers the canvas.

It starts at 100 %. If the first selected clip's picture is within 1 % of the canvas's shape, it starts at 125 % instead, because at 100 % such a picture fills the canvas exactly and the frame has no room to move.

Zoom enlarges the picture, and so does putting a landscape picture on a tall canvas. A 1080p source on a 1080 × 1920 canvas is already enlarged ×1.78 at 100 %, which can look soft on a phone.

### Where Empty

Where Empty sets what the frame shows while there's nothing to follow.

| Choice | What shows |
| --- | --- |
| **Show Whole** | The whole picture, with a [blurred copy](#the-blurred-backgrounds-track) filling the canvas around it. This is the default. |
| **Center** | The middle of the picture, at the same zoom |

It's dimmed while Follow is **Center**.

### What's remembered

**Follow** and **Where Empty** are remembered for next time, and [Make Vertical Version](/framing/make-vertical-version/) shares them. They're saved when you choose **Follow**, even if you then stop the analysis, and never on **Cancel**. **Zoom** isn't remembered.

## The summary

Under the controls, the sheet says what **Follow** will do. It updates as you change a control, and after you leave the Zoom field.

| The sheet says | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| "Frames 2 clips." | How many clips will change. |
| "Adds a Backgrounds track for the blurred copy." | Some of the framing shows the whole picture, so a [blurred copy](#the-blurred-backgrounds-track) goes behind it. |
| "Adds 1 more track behind it where clips overlap." | Two selected clips overlap in time, so their copies need separate tracks. |
| "2 actions re-eased at a cut." | A shot change landed inside actions the clip already had, and each was split there and eased again on either side. See [It starts from the whole picture](#it-starts-from-the-whole-picture). |
| "1 action carries a framing move." | A move couldn't fit between the clip's own actions, so one of them carries it. |
| "Clip 3 is already framed this way." | That clip wouldn't change. |
| "Clip 3: …" | That clip can't be framed, and this is why. See [Clips it cannot frame](#clips-it-cannot-frame). |
| "Reading the analysis…" | Frame Job is loading what it found earlier. **Follow** is dimmed until it's done. |
| "Finds the faces, people and shot changes in 1 file on this Mac first, then frames 1 clip." | The [analysis comes first](#analysis-first). |

**Follow** is dimmed when nothing would change.

"Clip 3" uses Frame Job's own number for the clip, which isn't its position on the timeline.

## Analysis first

When the clips haven't been analysed, choosing **Follow** closes the sheet and opens the [Analyzing sheet](/projects/media-analysis/#the-analyzing-sheet) while Frame Job finds what it needs on your Mac. It then frames the clips by itself.

The Analyzing sheet has a row for each file and each kind of analysis: **Shot changes**, **Faces**, and **People and salient regions**. Only the part of each file the clip plays is read, plus a second either side.

**Stop** changes nothing. **Center** needs no analysis, so it frames at once.

Frame Job beeps and frames nothing in these cases, and says why at the foot of the inspector:

| The inspector says | What happened |
| --- | --- |
| "the project changed while Follow Subject was analyzing, so nothing was framed. Choose Follow Subject again." | The project changed, or you went into or out of a nest, while the analysis ran. What was found is kept, so a second try doesn't start over. |
| "The faces analysis of “interview.mov” failed: …" | An analysis couldn't finish. The sentence names the kind and the file. |

## It starts from the whole picture

Each clip is framed from the whole picture. Its own positions and scales are replaced, both the clip's base values and any an action sets. An action left with nothing to do is removed. The clip's volume and its other actions stay, and so does its crop, which the frame stays inside.

The moves then fit around the actions that remain:

- A move goes in a gap between them.
- A move that would overlap an action starts up to 0.5 s earlier to clear it.
- A move that still can't clear is carried by the action it overlaps, along that action's curve.
- A shot change that lands inside an action cuts it in three around the one-frame cut. A steady (linear) action plays as it did, and an eased one is eased again on each side.
- A speed action, or an action a trim left running past the clip's end, is never cut. It carries the change instead.

## How following moves

The frame never leaves the picture, so it doesn't show past the picture's edge while it follows.

### Which subject it follows

When several faces or people are in view, Frame Job scores each on how steadily it's there, how big it is and how central it is, over the second either side and within the shot.

It stays with its choice. Another subject takes over only after scoring at least 25 % better for 2 s, so two similar faces don't trade the frame back and forth. With **Subject**, a person's body stands in for their face while the face is turned away.

Only the first eight of each kind in a sample count. For faces, that's the eight furthest left.

### Where the subject sits

| Subject | Where it sits |
| --- | --- |
| A face | In the middle of the frame, or 38 % of the way down on a frame taller than wide, leaving room below for the rest of the person |
| A person | With the top of their box 12 % of the way down the frame |
| A salient region | In the middle of the frame |

### Easing and staying put

The frame eases onto the subject and moves only when the subject leaves the middle of the frame, so a speaker who sways stays put. The middle counts as 15 % of the frame's width and 12 % of its height either side.

A move travels at 0.8 frame widths a second and takes at least 0.4 s. No move starts within 0.5 s of the last one's end, unless the subject has left the frame altogether.

### At a shot change

The frame cuts with the picture, landing on the first frame of the new shot. It's placed on where the subject sits over the new shot's first second. No move runs across a cut.

### When the subject is lost

The frame holds for a second, so a blink or a turned head changes nothing. It then follows someone else in the shot if there's anyone. If not, it eases over 0.8 s to your [Where Empty](#where-empty) choice.

It comes back once a subject has been in view for 0.6 s.

A clip with nobody in view during its first second opens on Where Empty. A clip with nothing to follow at all stays on Where Empty for its whole length.

### Two people

The frame holds two faces or two people together when both fit in it. Each box is widened by 15 % before they're tested against the frame. Salient regions aren't paired.

## The blurred Backgrounds track

Where the frame shows the whole picture, the canvas shows around it. So a blurred copy of the clip goes on a new track named **Backgrounds** at the back, for the clip's whole length. That's the same copy [**Clip ▸ Add Blurred Background**](/canvas/backgrounds/#blurred-background) makes: picture only, filling the canvas.

No track is added when no clip needs one, which is always the case with **Center** for Follow or Where Empty. Where two selected clips overlap in time, the second copy goes on a further new track behind Backgrounds.

A clip with speed actions keeps them on its copy, so the copy shows the same frames.

## Every move is an action

Every move is an ordinary action on the clip's [action lane](/motion/action-lane/). To nudge where a frame ends, select the action and [drag the picture on the canvas](/motion/edit-an-action/#edit-on-the-canvas). You can move, resize or remove it as you would any other.

## Undo

**Edit ▸ Undo Follow Subject** takes the whole command back in one step, every clip and track included. What was found stays in the cache.

## Screen recordings are skipped

A screen recording Frame Job made, with its [cursor file](/recording/cursor-files/), isn't followed by faces, because a face on a screen isn't what the viewer is looking at. Follow Subject leaves it unanalysed and lists it under the summary:

> Clip 3: clip 3's media has a cursor file, so it follows the cursor, not faces; frame it with cursor, center, fit or keep

Of those, the sheet offers **Center**. [Make Vertical Version](/framing/make-vertical-version/) follows the pointer instead, and an agent can [follow it too](/framing/reframe-clip/).

## Clips it cannot frame

A selected movie clip that can't be followed gets a line under the summary, and the others are still framed. With no clip left to frame, the summary shows only those lines and **Follow** stays dimmed.

| Clip | The line says | What you can do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| On a matte track | "clip 3 is on a matte track, which framing would move; only keep reframes it" | Change the track's [matte setting](/canvas/matte-tracks/) or move the clip |
| Cut by a matte | "clip 3 is cut by the matte on track 7, which framing would move it out of; only keep reframes it" | The same |
| Rotated | "clip 3 is turned 15°, and framing works on an upright picture; only keep reframes it" | Set its [rotation](/canvas/transform/) back to 0° |
| Turned by an action | "clip 3's action 12 turns it, and framing works on an upright picture; only keep reframes it" | Take rotation out of [that action](/motion/edit-an-action/#take-a-property-out-of-the-action) |
| Spinning | "clip 3 spins in its motion, and framing works on an upright picture; only keep reframes it" | Remove the spin [preset](/motion/motion-presets/) |
| Cropped or scaled to nothing | "clip 3's crop or scale leaves no picture to frame" | Fix its [crop](/canvas/crop/) or scale |
| With a cursor file | See [above](#screen-recordings-are-skipped) | Choose **Center** |
| With no analysis under it | "clip 3 has no subjects to follow; analyze it first" | Lengthen the clip, or analyse its file again. A clip shorter than the gap between two samples can land here. |

"keep" and the other lowercase words in these lines are an agent's options. See [Reframe a clip (agents)](/framing/reframe-clip/).

A clip with nobody in it isn't one of these. It's framed on your [Where Empty](#where-empty) choice.

When an analysis has to run first, the sheet can't list these lines yet. Afterwards the clips that can be framed are framed, and the rest stay as they were with no message. If none can be, Frame Job beeps and shows the lines at the foot of the inspector.

## Good to know

- If a clip's file is missing or can't be read, the summary says so and **Follow** stays dimmed. [Relink it](/projects/relink-media/), or choose **Center**, which doesn't read the file.
- Follow Subject doesn't frame stills or pictures. [Make Vertical Version](/framing/make-vertical-version/) centres those.
- Running Follow Subject again on a clip whose frame shows the whole picture adds another Backgrounds track and another copy, and the first copy stays. Undo the first run, or delete the old copy.
- Inside a [nest](/editing/nests/), the nest's canvas is the canvas, and the Backgrounds track goes in the nest.
- A clip's speed, speed ramps and reversal are all taken into account, so the frame moves with what the clip shows.

## With an agent

`reframe_clip` frames one clip at a time. Follow Subject is that tool run on each selected clip, starting from the whole picture, with a Backgrounds track behind.

An agent has more choices than the sheet. It can show the whole picture, rescale a clip from the canvas it was made for, follow a recorded pointer or follow whoever's talking, and it can compose the framing into a clip's own moves instead of replacing them. See [Reframe a clip (agents)](/framing/reframe-clip/) and [Tools: framing and vertical](/mcp/tools-framing/).

## Related

- [Subjects in the picture](/framing/what-is-found/)
- [Show Subjects](/framing/show-subjects/)
- [Make Vertical Version](/framing/make-vertical-version/)
- [Backgrounds](/canvas/backgrounds/)
- [Actions](/motion/actions/)

18	Frame Job looks at the picture ten times a second of the file's own time, so a clip you've slowed down or sped up doesn't change what's found. It keeps three things from each look.
19	
20	### Faces
21	
22	Each face's box, how it's turned, and how open the mouth is. Faces in a sample are listed from left to right. See [Faces](/projects/media-analysis/#faces) under media analysis.
23	
24	### People
25	
26	Each person's head and shoulders, as a box. A person's box can stand in for their face while the face can't be found.
27	
28	### Salient regions
29	
30	The parts of the picture the eye goes to first, as boxes. In a talking-head shot this is usually the speaker. On a slide it's often the text. See [People and salient regions](/projects/media-analysis/#people-and-salient-regions) under media analysis.
31	
32	[Show Subjects](/framing/show-subjects/) draws all three over the preview, so you can see what Frame Job has to work with.
33	
34	## Boxes, not people
...
38	[Follow Subject](/framing/follow-subject/#which-subject-it-follows) works out who's who for itself each time it plans, from how the boxes overlap from one sample to the next. That reasoning isn't kept, and it stops at a shot change. Someone who leaves the shot for more than a second and comes back counts as someone new.
39	
40	## When a file is analysed
41	
42	Importing a file doesn't analyse its picture. A file is analysed when something asks for it:
43	
44	- **Clip ▸ Follow Subject…**
45	- **File ▸ Make Vertical Version…**
46	- [**Clip ▸ Switch by Speaker…**](/multicam/one-microphone/), when it cuts from faces
47	- An agent, with `get_media_analysis`, `reframe_clip` or `make_vertical_version`
48	
49	Follow Subject, Make Vertical Version and `reframe_clip` ask only for the part of the file each clip plays, plus a second either side. **View ▸ Show Subjects** never asks, so turning it on costs nothing.
50	
51	Analysis runs in the background and keeps what it has found if it's stopped. Asking again continues from there, and a part that's already been analysed isn't read again. What's found is kept in the project's cache, so a file is only analysed once.
52	
53	[On-device media analysis](/projects/media-analysis/#analysis-happens-on-demand) covers this in full, including [the Analyzing sheet](/projects/media-analysis/#the-analyzing-sheet) and [how background jobs run](/projects/media-analysis/#analysis-runs-in-the-background).
54	
55	## What uses it
56	
57	| Feature | What it uses |

18	Frame Job looks at the picture ten times a second of the file's own time, so a clip you've slowed down or sped up doesn't change what's found. It keeps three things from each look.
19	
20	### Faces
21	
22	Each face's box, how it's turned, and how open the mouth is. Faces in a sample are listed from left to right. See [Faces](/projects/media-analysis/#faces) under media analysis.
23	
24	### People
25	
26	Each person's head and shoulders, as a box. A person's box can stand in for their face while the face can't be found.
27	
28	### Salient regions
29	
30	The parts of the picture the eye goes to first, as boxes. In a talking-head shot this is usually the speaker. On a slide it's often the text. See [People and salient regions](/projects/media-analysis/#people-and-salient-regions) under media analysis.
31	
32	[Show Subjects](/framing/show-subjects/) draws all three over the preview, so you can see what Frame Job has to work with.
33	
34	## Boxes, not people
...
38	[Follow Subject](/framing/follow-subject/#which-subject-it-follows) works out who's who for itself each time it plans, from how the boxes overlap from one sample to the next. That reasoning isn't kept, and it stops at a shot change. Someone who leaves the shot for more than a second and comes back counts as someone new.
39	
40	## When a file is analysed
41	
42	Importing a file doesn't analyse its picture. A file is analysed when something asks for it:
43	
44	- **Clip ▸ Follow Subject…**
45	- **File ▸ Make Vertical Version…**
46	- [**Clip ▸ Switch by Speaker…**](/multicam/one-microphone/), when it cuts from faces
47	- An agent, with `get_media_analysis`, `reframe_clip` or `make_vertical_version`
48	
49	Follow Subject, Make Vertical Version and `reframe_clip` ask only for the part of the file each clip plays, plus a second either side. **View ▸ Show Subjects** never asks, so turning it on costs nothing.
50	
51	Analysis runs in the background and keeps what it has found if it's stopped. Asking again continues from there, and a part that's already been analysed isn't read again. What's found is kept in the project's cache, so a file is only analysed once.
52	
53	[On-device media analysis](/projects/media-analysis/#analysis-happens-on-demand) covers this in full, including [the Analyzing sheet](/projects/media-analysis/#the-analyzing-sheet) and [how background jobs run](/projects/media-analysis/#analysis-runs-in-the-background).
